title: Keep producer work on deadline and resume it on retry
summary: When the producer stage hits its deadline, keep the worktree edits and a progress note, record the job as timed out (not failed), and have `athena retry` resume from the kept work with the note. Status shows timed out versus failed. Producer stage only, as the user narrowed earlier. Audience: the Athena operator who loses 20–30 minutes per timeout. This is the first small step only; the deadline length and planning splits are untouched.

defaults_applied.how: Tests added; cargo test and clippy pass.
Criteria check the timeout, kept edits and resume happening via tests.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy, fmt --check.
Criteria check that a retry resumes from kept work.
Docs and changelog written for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Scope stays as the user narrowed the earlier attempt: producer stage only; no verifier-stage timeouts, no multi-part planning, no deadline length change.
Previous deliverable list is a good starting point; the exact files are confirmed by the producer while reading the code.
Timed-out is a new outcome value; old records with killed or failed outcomes must deserialize unchanged.
Keeping the partial diff means leaving the job worktree intact and writing a progress note file listing changed files and last activity.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test with the fake agent exceeds a short producer deadline after editing files. Afterwards the edits remain in the job worktree, a progress note listing the changed files exists, and the job is recorded as timed out, not failed. Run: cargo test.
A test retries a timed-out job. The new producer starts from the kept worktree (not a clean checkout) and is given the progress note naming the earlier changed files. Run: cargo test.
Status output distinguishes a timed-out job from a failed one, and the deadline reason (e.g. 'deadline of 1800s reached') is kept in the record. Run: cargo test.
A test shows existing records with killed or failed outcomes still deserialize unchanged, and a job that finishes in time behaves as before. Run: cargo test.
The new timed-out outcome is documented and CHANGELOG.md mentions the change.
cargo test, cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check all pass with no new warnings.

departures: Cost and time are raised because the earlier attempt hit the 1800s deadline and the change spans several crates.
urgent_reason: Retries of timed-out producer jobs currently redo 20–30 minutes of lost work; keeping it cuts redo-work retries and timeouts.
